newsitem.title: CANADA: Bre-X says Busang find possibly overstated.
newsitem.headline: Bre-X says Busang find possibly overstated.

text.p: Bre-X Minerals Ltd. said on Wednesday there appeared to be a "strong possibility" that the potential gold resources in the Busang gold mining project in Indonesia have been overstated due to invalid samples and assays of those samples.
The Indonesian site had been viewed as one of the world's richest gold deposits.

Bre-X said that "there appears to be a strong possibility that the potential gold resources on the Busang project in East Kalimantan, Indonesia have been overstated because of invalid samples and assaying of those samples."
Freeport-McMoRan Copper & Gold Inc., which has a 15 percent stake in Busang, said earlier Wednesday that its own tests of the Busang II site indicate insignificant gold amounts.
Bre-X said its statement was based on advice from Strathcona Mineral Services Ltd., an independent Canadian mining industry consultant.

Bre-X said its board of directors retained Strathcona last week to review and comment on the technical programmes carried out to date by Bre-X. It was also requested to review the due diligence programme being conducted by Freeport-McMoRan.
"Strathcona has recommended to Bre-X that an audit be conducted of the drilling and sampling programmes done by both Bre-X and FCX (Freeport)," the statement said.

"This audit will include the drilling of further core samples and will take approximately four weeks. Bre-X has accepted Strathcona's recommendation and has advised Strathcona to immediately proceed with this audit programme," Bre-X said.
Shares in the Calgary-based gold prospector were halted before the start of trading on the Toronto Stock Exchange.

Bre-X's stock has been under pressure since an Indonesian newspaper report last week questioned the size and viability of the Busang gold site. Investors have also been skittish over the mysterious death last week of a co-discoverer of the Busang site.
